explanation: Two tape bars hold the same pieces a and b in different orders. The top bar is a then b; the bottom bar swaps them to b then a — yet both reach the exact same right edge, which is why a + b = b + a (the commutative property). The dashed green line marks that shared total and the twin sweeping dots prove both rows fill to the same length. Slide a and b to change the pieces, and use the step slider to flip the order so you can watch the total stay put.
bullets: Commutative: swapping the order of addends never changes the sum.
The two tapes hold the same pieces, so they end at the same total.
Properties like this let you reorder and regroup to compute easily.
